attempts.summary: On node1 (AlmaLinux 9), built a local RPM repository from packages downloaded to local storage, served it over HTTP from the node's own IP, blackholed the real AlmaLinux mirror/repo hostnames to simulate remote-repo unreachability, and successfully installed the `tree` package from the local repo only. Then executed the mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured a healthy baseline (boot ID, repo data checksums, HTTP 200 from local repo), rebooted node1 via `systemctl reboot`, confirmed the boot ID changed, verified repo data/config survived, restarted the local HTTP server (an ephemeral process, not a persistent unit), reconfirmed the local-repo install path still worked post-reboot while remotes were still blackholed, and finally restored normal networking.
